thread:
Jordan: heads-up — seeing a ~2.7% parse failure spike on canary for nova-int8-v2 when invoking tool calls. started ~06:12 UTC, coincides with the int8 rollout.
Priya: can you paste an example failure payload/log?
Jordan: sure, one of the logs:
```
ERROR json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
model output (truncated): '{"action":"create_ticket","args":{"title":"OOM on xla",' \n... '\u0000\n'
```
Jordan: lots of outputs end with odd control chars or a trailing "..." and then non-json text. Also some responses look like NDJSON with a stray comma before EOF.
Sam: hmm. did canary change batch_size / kv cache / streaming boundaries?
Jordan: canary config: batch_size=8, kv_cache=true, streaming=enabled, quant_profile=ptq-int8. Baseline float canary had batch_size=4.
Priya: kv cache + bigger batch could alter token alignment on suffixes. any tokenizer diffs between float and int8 builds?
Jordan: tokenization model build was identical AFAICT. but the quant conversion pipeline added a post-process pass that strips some control bytes — might be the culprit.
Lina: immediate mitigation: route canary traffic to nova-fp16 until we root cause. also add a parser-rescue hook that tries to strip trailing control chars and rerun soft-json-lint before marking failure.
Sam: +1 for runtime rescue. we should also add a fallback to the float model if parse fails after N retries (and count those as soft-failures in telemetry).
infra-bot: Deploy 4291000015: rollback route for canary -> nova-fp16 initiated by @lina
Priya: I'll run a repro locally with batch_size=8 kv_cache=true and the exact quant artifact. any quick reproduce snippet?
Jordan: small request body we used:
```
POST /v1/invoke
{
  "model": "nova-int8-v2",
  "input": "<prompt that triggers toolcall>",
  "stream": false,
  "max_tokens": 256
}
```
Jordan: telemetry: parse_failure_rate canary = 2.7%, baseline = 0.02% (last 24h). token-level entropy for suffix tokens up 30% vs baseline.
Sam: sounds like suffix generation got noisier. possible causes: quant kernel edge-case, failure in continuous-batching token boundary handling, or kv-cache alignment bug.
Lina: action items:
- Priya: reproduce locally and dump raw token ids + bytes (due EOD)
- Sam: prototype a parser-rescue that strips control chars and retries parse with soft_parse=true (PR by tomorrow)
- Jordan: keep canary routed to fp16 until we confirm (done via infra-bot)
- Infra: add short-term alert for parse_rate > 0.5% for canary models
Priya: got it. I'll attach token dumps to this thread once I have them :eyes:
Jordan: thanks. if we confirm quant post-process introduced the bad bytes we should roll a tiny re-export and re-run canary with same batching.
Sam: also add an eval harness for funcall compliance that runs on quant artifacts (small suite: malformed-suffix, ndjson-trailer, control-bytes) so this doesn't regress silently.
Lina: agreed. tagging @product-devex to add a canary check to onboarding checklist.
Jordan: nice. closing for now — will update once Priya posts traces. :thumbsup:
